'''Hafeez Hoorani''' or '''Hafeez-ur-Rehman Hoorani''' or '''Hafeez R. Hoorani''' is a Pakistani [[particle physicist]], with a specialisation in [[accelerator physics]], and a [[research scientist]] at the [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite news| author =Staff Reporter| title =Pakistani scientist appointed SESAME Director Science| newspaper =Pakistan Times| location =[[Islamabad]], Pakistan| url =http://www.Pakistantimes.net/2007/01/09/top10.htm| url-status =usurped| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20070302174929/http://www.pakistantimes.net/2007/01/09/top10.htm| archive-date =2 March 2007| df =dmy-all}}
</ref> Hoorani is working at the [[National Center for Physics]], with research focus in [[elementary particle physics]] and [[high energy physics]].<ref>{{citation needed|date=July 2017}}{{Cite web
  | last = Courier
  | first = CERN
  | author-link =European Organization for Nuclear Research 
  | title =A unique experience
  | publisher = CERN
  | year = 2008
  | url = http://public.web.cern.ch/public/en/People/Hoorani-en.html
  | access-date =20 January 2010}}
</ref> 
Until the end of 2013, he served as scientific director of [[International Centre for Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science Applications in the Middle East (SESAME)]] and is now research associate at the [[Riazuddin National Center for Nuclear Physics|National Center for Nuclear Physics]], [[Islamabad]].<ref>{{Cite web| last =SESAME| first =International Centre for Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science Applications in the Middle East| author-link =International Centre for Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science Applications in the Middle East| title =SESAME Directorate| url =http://www.sesame.org.jo/directorate/directorate.aspx| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110928121151/http://www.sesame.org.jo/directorate/directorate.aspx| archive-date =28 September 2011| df =dmy-all}}</ref>

He has served as a [[full professor]] of [[high energy physics]] at the [[National Center for Physics]] where he heads a group building the [[ZEUS (particle detector)|muon chamber]] for the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|Compact Muon Solenoid detector]]. He also supervised two PhD students during his stay at the [[National Center for Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web
 |last        = NCP
 |first       = National Center for Physics
 |author-link  = National Center for Physics
 |title       = PhD Students of NCP Visited CERN
 |publisher   = National Center for Physics
 |url         = http://www.ncp.edu.pk/newsletters/Vol1-1/ncpvol1-1_details.htm
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20081210103648/http://www.ncp.edu.pk/newsletters/Vol1-1/ncpvol1-1_details.htm
 |archive-date = 10 December 2008
 |df          = dmy-all
}}
</ref>

==Education==
Hoorani was born in [[Karachi]] and received his early education from there. He attended [[Karachi University]] in 1976 and received his [[B.Sc. (Hons)|BSc with Honors]] in physics in 1980, followed by his MSc in [[particle physics]] from the same institution in 1982. On a KU's awarded scholarship, Hoorani went to [[Burnaby]], Canada where he attended [[Simon Fraser University]].<ref>{{Citation| last =Australian Synchronton| title =Dr Hafeez-ur-Rehman Hoorani:CERN – European Organization for Nuclear Research| date =7 September 2009| url =http://www.asnevents.com.au/sri09/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=61&Itemid=96}}{{dead link|date=October 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
</ref> In October 1986, he received his PhD {{citation needed|date=July 2017}} in [[High Energy Physics|Experimental High Energy Physics]] under the supervision of Dr. David H. Boal, writing his thesis on ''Numerical Solution for Hydrodynamic Equations For the Quark-Gluon Plasma''.<ref>{{Cite journal
  | last =Hoorani 
  | first = Hafeez
  | title = Numerical Solution for Hydrodynamic Equations For the Quark-Gluon Plasma 
  | publisher = Department of Physics: [[Simon Fraser University]] 
  | location =[[Burnaby]] (BBY), [[British Columbia]], Canada 
  | pages =1–105   
  | date =21 October 1986
  | url =http://ir.lib.sfu.ca/bitstream/1892/7346/1/b15314091.pdf 
  }}
</ref>

== CERN ==
In 1987, Hoorani joined the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] where he continued his research into [[Quark–gluon plasma]] and published a brief journal on ''Production of J/ψ IK Quark-Gloun Plasma'' in February 1988.<ref>{{Cite journal 
  | last =Hoorani 
  | first =Hafeez 
  | title =Production of J/ψ IK Quark-Gloun Plasma 
  | publisher =[[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) 
  | date =February 1988 
  | url =http://streaming.ictp.trieste.it/preprints/P/88/027.pdf 
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110722055705/http://streaming.ictp.trieste.it/preprints/P/88/027.pdf 
  | archive-date =22 July 2011 
  | url-status =dead 
  }}</ref> Hoorani joined CERN in 1989 where he carried out a large amount of research at CERN's [[Large Electron–Positron Collider]] or LEP. In 1999, he returned to Pakistan for a short visit where he successfully convinced the [[Government of Pakistan]] to set up a group working on different aspects of the [[Large Hadron Collider]] at the [[National Center for Physics]]. Due to his efforts, in 2000 [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (led by [[nuclear physicist]] Dr. [[Ishfaq Ahmad]]) signed an agreement with CERN. This agreement opened the door for [[:Category:Pakistani physicists|Pakistani physicists]] to collaborate with CERN's [[particle physics]] project.<ref>{{Cite web
  | last =Pakistani  
  | first =Welder  
  | title =Hafeez Hoorani 
  | date = 25 April 2009
  | url = https://welderPakistani.blogspot.com/2009/04/hafeez-hoorani.html
  }}</ref> His current research area is the development of gaseous detectors for the hadron collider.
